To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the motor system of cats is able to preserve task level variables during locomotion in the presence of substantial muscle denervation by means of neural adaptation, not by intrinsic properties of the system.
the immediate effects of paralysis on locomotion are not consistent with the idea that the motor system uses feedback regulation or intrinsic mechanisms to preserve task level variables.
the motor system is capable, within seconds, of preserving task level variables such locomotor trajectory and limb length in the face of denervation and fasciotomy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding how the nervous system regulates locomotion.
the role of the central nervous system (CNS) in the control of locomotion.
the control of locomotor behavior.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

, at least during locomotion, the nervous system has the capacity to adapt the motor commands in such a way that the task level variables of the limbs are maintained in the face of substantial perturbations.

the preservation of the limb trajectory is not due to intrinsic properties of the muscle-tendon complex or due to short term feedback mechanisms, but that it is due to a long term neural adaptation process.
the motor system does not compensate for paralysis of major muscle group(s) during locomotion by rapid feedback regulation or intrinsic mechanical mechanisms.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the motor system is able to compensate for major muscle paralysis during locomotion, but this compensation is not immediate and is not accomplished by online feedback control or intrinsic properties of musculotendon actuators.

the motor system is capable not only of preserving task level variables in the presence of paralysis of major muscles, but also of adjusting these variables to compensate for disruption in the mechanical properties of the limb.
the motor system is capable to preserve the task level variables during locomotion in the face of muscle paralysis by the adjustment of kinematics of joints.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the motor system is capable, in the face of major disruptions to the musculoskeletal apparatus, of preserving the trajectories of limb level variables during locomotion.
the nervous system is able to preserve the trajectories of task level variables in response to paralysis of the major extensors during locomotion in the decerebrate cat.

, in the face of substantial changes in limb mechanics, the motor system is capable, within seconds, of preserving task level variables such that the limb trajectory remains similar to that observed in the normal state.
